content:
The Bluetooth SIG ratified the Bluetooth 7.0 specification on November 3, 2026, with the highlight of the new Bluetooth Core specification being optional support for HDT (High Data Throughput), delivering up to 7.5 Mbps bitrate. We first covered HDT in 2025 when initial/early support was implemented into the Ceva-Waves Links200 multi-protocol platform IP, and followed last September with the Realtek RTL8773J Bluetooth 7-ready Cortex-M55/M33 microcontroller. The main news is that the specification for Bluetooth 7.0 and the associated HDT feature is officially ratified/adopted. Bluetooth 7.0 highlights: Bluetooth High Data Throughput (HDT) introduces a new Bluetooth LE physical layer that increases the maximum Bluetooth bit rate to 7.5 Mbps while improving wireless efficiency and robustness. The higher bitrate is enabled by a combination of higher-order modulation, convolutional forward error correction, synchronization enhancements, adaptive rate selection, and enhanced packet architectures.
